title: e says /e/
parentNote: Today is the fifth vowel, and that means it is the last one — after e your child has met a, e, i, o and u, the whole set, and can sound out most short words they meet on a page. It also hands them the little joining words that forty days of stories have had to do without: then, went, get, let. The wobble to expect is that e sits right between a and i in the mouth, so bed comes out bad and pet comes out pit. Say the two words back to back yourself — bed, bad — and let them hear that only the middle moved; the pairs in the middle of today's lesson are there for exactly that. If they are tired, stop after the story. Today is a big one.

activities.mouthCue: Your mouth opens a little and your tongue sits flat, halfway between a and i.

activities.text: The red hen sat on a nest in the shed.
Ted did get up and then let the dog in.
Jen fell in the mud and Ted did help.

activities.title: The hen in the bed
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Ted got a pet hen and the hen is red.
At dusk the hen went in the shed and sat on the bed.
Ted did beg and beg but the hen did not get up.
Then the hen did get up and left an egg on the bed!
Ted got the egg and did grin. The hen can rest in the bed.
